title: Findings that repeat from one State review to the next
question: The State fiscal-crisis team asked the district the same questions in 2022, 2024 and 2026. Which failings were still there each time?
finding: The State team answered "no" (a failing) to 54 questions in 2022, 64 in 2024 and 60 in 2026. 16 questions were answered "no" in all three reviews, among them: audit findings left uncorrected; staffing records not used to build the budget; actual revenue and spending out of line with the budget; deficiencies named in State oversight letters not addressed; no board-approved plan to control transfers from the general fund; falling enrolment; school buildings not fully used. 10 of the 20 sections had more failings in 2026 than in 2022; between 2024 and 2026 the count rose in budget development and adoption, charter schools, deficit spending (unrestricted general fund), general fund - current year, information systems and data management, leadership and stability, special education.
how: Section counts are taken from the comparison table the State team printed as Appendix A of its 13 August 2026 report. The count of questions failed in all three reviews is this project's own reading: each 2026 question answered "no" is matched to the question in the same section of the 2022 and 2024 reports that shares at least half its distinctive words, and counted when both of those were also answered "no".
limits: The team reworded, added and dropped questions between reviews, so a match by wording can miss a question or pair two that differ; the section table is the team's own and does not have that problem. A "no" on falling enrolment is a fact about the city, not a failing of management. Each review is a snapshot at one budget report; the district certified its own budget as sound again in June 2026, after the period the latest review covers.
